coach.name: Kahil Fennell
coach.notes: Hired as WMU's 16th head coach after two seasons at UTRGV (35-29: 16-14, then 19-14 and third in the Southland; UTRGV had won six games the year before he arrived). Former assistant at Louisville and BYU. AP story says the hire was announced on a Saturday (March 21, 2026); Wikipedia lists March 23, 2026. Replaced Dwayne Stephens, fired March 10, 2026 after a 10-21 season (42-84 in four seasons); WMU has had eight straight losing seasons. AD Dan Bartholomae praised his 'track record of recruiting, developing and connecting with student-athletes.' Contract terms not found. Mid-Major Madness calls him one of its favorite hires of the cycle, noting he lifted UTRGV to 117th in KenPom. Turned over the entire roster (14 newcomers) and brought eight new staff; assistants Dustin Yoder, Bobby Horodyski, Cam Clark, Michael Provenzano; DOBO Adam Howard; player development Manny Patterson.

previews.title: 2026-27 MAC Men's Basketball Preview
previews.author: Sam Federman
previews.projected_finish: Listed 10th in the article's order; author says he would have WMU closer to 6th
previews.summary: Federman calls Fennell one of his favorite hires of the cycle after Fennell raised UTRGV to 117th in KenPom in two years. Fennell brought UTRGV guards Jaylen Washington and Julien Gomez with him and added Lamar transfer Rob Lee Jr. in the backcourt. Wings Tanner Hayhurst (6-6) and Isaac Finlinson (6-8) supply size and shooting, and 6-11 international Janis Jünemann can anchor the middle. The author thinks the team is ranked too low.

player_claims.claim: 6-11 international player who can anchor the middle.

previews.title: 2026-27 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season
previews.projected_finish: 8th of 12 in MAC preseason coaches poll (58 points)
previews.summary: Western Michigan was picked eighth with 58 points, behind Bowling Green (63) and ahead of Eastern Michigan (56), Buffalo, Ball State and Central Michigan. No WMU player made the preseason All-MAC teams. Fennell is one of four new MAC head coaches (with Akron's Dustin Ford, Ball State's Chris Capko and Eastern Michigan's Billy Donlon).

previews.title: Brand new WMU basketball roster feature two local players
previews.author: News Channel 3 staff
previews.summary: Fennell replaced the entire roster with 14 new Broncos. The piece highlights two with local ties: Portage Central product Ben Johnson, who scored more than 1,000 career points for the Mustangs, and Grand Rapids native Ramere Draper, a former Kalamazoo Valley CC standout who averaged 19.4 points, 6.9 rebounds and 3.5 assists in his final KVCC season.

player_claims.claim: Portage Central standout with 1,000-plus career points.
Grand Rapids native; ex-KVCC standout who averaged 19.4 ppg, 6.9 rpg, 3.5 apg in his final season there.

previews.title: Men's Basketball Begins New Era with First Summer Workout
previews.summary: First workout under Fennell on June 9 with an all-new 14-man roster, many via the transfer portal, and eight new staff members. Fennell: 'Overall, today was really ugly... A little bit of it was paralysis by analysis,' adding 'They aren't used to the physicality, but we don't want to risk injuries.' Players featured: Augustinas Kiudulas (Lithuania), Janis Jünemann (Latvia), Isaac Finlinson (Hawaii transfer), Ben Johnson (Portage), Jordan Sigmon (Detroit), Ramere Draper (Grand Rapids), Rob Lee Jr. (Flint).

player_claims.claim: From St. George, Utah; previously at Hawaii.

previews.title: Men's Basketball Releases 2026-27 Non-Conference Schedule
previews.summary: Non-conference slate: Nov 2 at Old Dominion (MAC-SBC Challenge), Nov 5 vs Kalamazoo College (home opener), Nov 8 vs Campbell, Nov 12 at Purdue Fort Wayne, Nov 15 at Southern Indiana, Nov 20 at Mount St. Mary's, Nov 25 vs Grace Christian, Dec 18 vs Great Lakes Christian, Dec 22 at USC, Feb 6 MAC-SBC Challenge home game. MAC play opens with a four-game stretch in early December and resumes at Akron Jan 2. Fennell: 'This is a very challenging slate that takes us on the road to some big-time opponents.'

recent_news.headline: WMU routs Kalamazoo College 99-52 for Fennell's first win
recent_news.detail: WMU made 17 threes (one short of the program record) on a program-record 43 attempts, outrebounded Kalamazoo 63-30, and got 65 bench points with 12 of 13 players scoring. Mason Bendinger 22 (9-of-12), Jordan Sigmon 15, Augustinas Kiudulas 11, Rob Lee Jr. 11 (three 3s), Ramere Draper 10, Janis Jünemann 11 rebounds. Record 1-1.
